name: Jeroham
overview: Jeroham is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Azariah, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 23:1. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details in Scripture. His identity is closely tied to his role as a progenitor within the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroham means 'he will be compassionate,' reflecting a Hebrew origin. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful attribute that may suggest character or divine favor.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Jeroham as the father of Azariah, establishing a direct paternal relationship. No other family connections are documented beyond this relationship in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroham's significance in Scripture is connected to his son Azariah, who appears in the context of 2 Chronicles 23:1. While Jeroham himself is not the focus of major events, his mention serves to identify and authenticate Azariah's lineage, which is important in the biblical genealogical and leadership records. This connection highlights the biblical emphasis on family lines and heritage within God's providential plan.
